Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:38: And concerning the three keys, they explain, of blessed memory (Zohar, Midrash HaNe'elam, Vayera 116b): these three the Holy One, blessed be He, did not hand over to any agent. Rabbi Simon said: come and see the power of the Holy One, blessed be He - at one and the same time He revives the dead, brings down to Sheol and raises up, causes the lights to shine, grows grass, fattens the produce, remembers the barren, gives sustenance, helps the poor, supports the falling, straightens the bent, removes kings and sets up kings - and all this at one time, in one moment and in one instant, which no agent in the world could do - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:39: And in Devarim Rabbah, Parashat "Vehaya Ki Tavo," on the verse (Deuteronomy 28:12), "the LORD shall open for you His good treasury," they elaborate on the virtue of the key of rain, saying it is equal to the resurrection of the dead. And it says there: another interpretation, "the LORD shall open for you" - Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov said, at the time the rains descend, commerce is blessed, as it is said (Deuteronomy 28:12), "to give the rain of your land in its season, and to bless all the work of your hands." The Rabbis say: even fish are blessed. Our Rabbis said, an incident, and so on. Another interpretation, "the LORD shall open for you" - come and see how great is the descent of rain: Rabbi Yehuda bar Yechezkel, when he would see the rains descending, would bless: may the name of Him who spoke and the world came into being be glorified, magnified, and blessed - He who appoints a thousand thousand thousands and myriad myriads of angels for every single drop that descends. Why? From here to the firmament is a journey of five hundred years, and the rains descend, and not one drop mixes with its fellow - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:40: And in the key of sustenance there is a contemplation, to understand and know that there is one Creator who watches over His particulars and knows their affairs for their good. And were I to elaborate on what I heard from my teachers concerning miracles that occurred to individual people concerning sustenance, through Elijah, of blessed memory, I would depart from the matter of this exposition - and here in Safed, one of them is still alive.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:41: And our master, Rabbi Shlomo Alkabetz HaLevi, may his light shine, instituted a prayer concerning sustenance, to be recited every day, and he wrote in it: You are the God who sustains from the horns of wild oxen to the eggs of lice, and no angel or prince has the power to sustain, provide for, and support Your provision, as written through David, Your servant (Psalms 145:15), "the eyes of all wait upon You, and You give them their food in its season"; "You open Your hand and satisfy every living thing with favor"; and it is written (ibid. 136:26), "who gives bread to all flesh, for His kindness is forever" - and this key is in Your hand, to refine and purify people, so that they trust in You and know that there is no savior besides You.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:42: And through this the verse "the eyes of all wait upon You," and so on, may be understood: "the eyes of all" includes all the worlds, upper and lower, that are below the Shechinah, for they all wait for their life and their flow from her - for even the angels nurse sustenance every day from above, and likewise the supernal souls, as explained in Parashat Terumah (Zohar 156b), and as we explained in the Gate of Holiness (chapter 15).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:43: Further, among God's kindnesses to man concerning his sustenance is giving him intellect, understanding, and knowledge to devise his livelihood through craft and stratagem - and this is what the verse says (Deuteronomy 8:18), "and you shall say in your heart, my power and the might of my hand have gotten me this wealth; but you shall remember the LORD your God, that it is He who gives you power to get wealth" - and Onkelos translates: "for He gives you counsel to acquire possessions."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:44: And so it says in Tanna Devei Eliyahu (Rabbah, 14): once I was passing from place to place and a man found me who had Scripture in hand but not Mishnah. He said to me: Rabbi, I will say one thing before you, and I fear you may be displeased. I said to him: Heaven forbid, if you ask me matters of Torah! He said to me: Rabbi, why is it written (Psalms 136:25), "who gives bread to all flesh," and it is written (Psalms 147:9), "who gives to the beast its food" - does a person not prepare his own bread? I said to him: this is the way of the world - one works with his hands, and the Holy One, blessed be He, blesses the work of his hands, as it is said (Deuteronomy 14:29), "that the LORD your God may bless you in all the work of your hand." Might one think he should sit idle? The verse teaches, "that you shall do." He said to me: this answer is the first approach I gave you. I said to him: my son, I will answer you further - go and learn from the fool, from whom wisdom has been taken, who cannot sustain himself for even one hour - therefore, when people lose their intellect, they are considered like a beast, an animal, or a bird, and the Holy One, blessed be He, distributes food to all who come into the world - to this point. This is brought in the Yalkut (Tehillim, Psalm 136, section 883), on the verse "who gives bread to all flesh."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:45: And in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah, section 15), it says, in these words: "who has cleft a channel for the flood" (Job 38:25) - Rabbi Berechiah said, there is a place where they call hair "sheifa" [flood/overflow]. There was an incident with a certain pious man who sat and expounded: there is not a single hair for which the Holy One, blessed be He, did not create its own separate follicle, so that no two would derive benefit from one another. The next day he sought to go out for his livelihood. They said to him: yesterday you sat and expounded that there is not a single hair for which the Holy One, blessed be He, did not create its own separate follicle, so that no two would derive benefit from one another - and now you seek to go out to search for your livelihood? Sit, and your Creator will provide for you. He heard, and sat, and his sustenance was provided for him - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:46: And in order to grasp the secret of the aforementioned discourse, you must know what is explained in the Tikkunim (67b), concerning the matter that "children, life, and sustenance do not depend on merit but on constellation [mazal]" - meaning that "mazal" refers to the first three [sefirot], and it says that "life" corresponds to Chochmah, "sustenance" corresponds to Binah, "children" corresponds to Da'at. And they say, of blessed memory (Tikkunei Zohar Chadash 103b): and from there [come] life, sustenance, and children - "life," for "wisdom preserves the life of him who has it"; "sustenance," "You open Your hand and satisfy every living thing with favor," and this is the supernal Imma; "children," a child of Yah - and this is the raised hand, Binah, whose letters are Y-H-V - to this point. This is found in manuscript, and in the printed edition it is along these lines, except that it says "life" is Chochmah and flows to the right thigh, "sustenance" is Binah and flows to the left thigh, and "children" is in Tiferet. And because sustenance flows from the side of Imma, the verse says (Job 38:25), "who has cleft a channel for the flood" - for the attribute of "Mi" [Binah] gives to every single follicle its own separate life-source - and therefore of her it is said (Psalms 55:23), "cast your burden upon the LORD," and so on.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:47: And it is possible to say that the three mentioned keys correspond to children, life, and sustenance, which depend on "mazal" - where the secret of the key explained in Parashat Bereshit lies - and therefore they are called "keys" and not handed over to any agent, because they depend on "mazal." And when you grasp what is explained in the Tikkunim concerning "You open Your hand" (Psalms 145:16), you will see and understand that three worlds are fittingly called three keys.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:48: And if sometimes a person suffers in attaining his livelihood, under pressing circumstances, he should know that the Holy One, blessed be He, wishes to chastise him with sufferings to atone for his sins. And the pious author of Chovot HaLevavot writes, also concerning the matter of food, when one discerns the food of creatures according to their kinds, concerning the fly's food for the spider. And along these lines, our Rabbis, of blessed memory, expound (Ketubot 49b, Tanchuma Eikev 2), concerning (Psalms 147:9), "to the young ravens which cry" - that the young are white and their parents do not recognize them, and the Holy One, blessed be He, has mercy on them and summons gnats from their own excrement, which enter their mouths.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:49: And what they expound (Midrash Tehillim, Psalm 42), on (Psalms 42:2), "as the deer pants for the water brooks" - in these words: "as the deer [ke-ayal] pants" - it does not say "as the doe" but "as the deer," a male term, [while] "pants" [ta'arog] is feminine - why? Rather, this doe, when she crouches upon the birthstool, is in distress and pants toward the Holy One, blessed be He, and He answers her and summons a serpent, and it bites her at the womb, and immediately the womb opens. So the sons of Korach cried out from their distress, that they not perish, and He answered them - therefore it says "as the deer pants." What is "for the water brooks"? The doe is the most pious of animals, and at a time when the animals are thirsty, they gather to the doe, and she digs and thrusts her horns into the ground and pants toward the Holy One, blessed be He, and He splits the deep for her and the waters rise for her - and this is "as the deer pants for the water brooks" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:50: And what it writes, "when she crouches upon the birthstool," and so on, "a serpent comes and bites her," and so on, is also explained by Rashbi, peace be upon him (Zohar, Parashat Beshalach 52b); and they further elaborate on the secret of the doe in Parashat Pinchas (249b); see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:51: Further, concerning the matter of discerning sustenances, is what Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Beshalach 61b), concerning the matter of the four sustenances - and we will copy his text in the Gate of Holiness, chapter 15 - and from there one may discern that man does not live by bread alone, but by everything that proceeds from the mouth of the LORD does man live.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:52: And through this you may settle what we see, that several penitents fast three days and three nights, and some have fasted four days and four nights, and some six, and did not die - and according to the way of nature, a doctor would say that his life is endangered - and along these lines, matters of self-mortification that penitents perform while remaining healthy - all this is divine assistance to them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:53: And it is possible that King David, peace be upon him, alluded to this when he said (Psalms 136:25), "who gives bread to all flesh, for His kindness is forever" - explaining that the Holy One, blessed be He, summons the food, called "bread," to all flesh according to its preparation: to one He summons bread, which is coarse food; to the sick, food according to their preparation; and to Torah scholars, according to their preparation - for the essential sustenance of Torah scholars is the Torah, as it is said (Proverbs 9:5), "come, eat of my bread." And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 45b), that when the Shechinah descends to bring flow to her children, to each one she brings down the sustenance fitting for him - to one she brings down the sustenance of Torah, which is the sustenance of the soul; to another she brings down the sustenance of the body - to each one according to his desire - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:54: Further, it is fitting that he consider how many miracles the Holy One, blessed be He, performed for him, and from how many dangers of death He saved him - for how many sick people reach the gates of death and are healed! And likewise, how many are threatened by robbers and are not killed.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:55: And sometimes the Holy One, blessed be He, performs a miracle for a person and he does not recognize it - as is brought in the Midrash, on the verse (Psalms 136:4), "to Him who alone does great wonders" - and they raised a difficulty: it is obvious that the Holy One, blessed be He, did everything alone, without any partner, Heaven forfend - and they answered, rather, He alone knows what wonders He performs. How so? A person is lying on his bed, and a serpent is before him on the ground; he goes to stand up, the serpent senses him and goes away from before him - and he does not know what wonders the Holy One, blessed be He, did for him, and who knows? The Holy One, blessed be He, [alone]. And so it says (Psalms 40:6), "many things You have done, O LORD my God - Your wonders and Your thoughts toward us - none can be compared to You; I would declare and speak of them, but they are more than can be told" - there is no way to elaborate Your praise, nor is it possible to recount Your wonders. Rabbi Elazar said: even the one for whom the miracle is performed does not recognize his own miracle, as it is said "alone." And as Rav Yosef expounded: what is written (Isaiah 12:1), "I will give thanks to You, O LORD, for though You were angry with me"? What does the verse speak of? Two men who went on a business trip; a thorn pierced one of them, and he began cursing and blaspheming; some days later he heard that his fellow's ship had sunk in the sea, and he began to give thanks and praise - therefore it says, "Your anger is turned away, and You comfort me" - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:56: Behold, among the things a person must discern with his mind, that it is from the providence of the Holy One, blessed be He, over man, is the matter of dreams - for through them a person's deeds are examined, as we copied the text of Rashbi, peace be upon him, in Parashat Chayei Sarah, in chapter 4 of the Gate of Holiness - for according to his deeds, so they show him in a dream, as Elihu said (Job 33:15-16), "in a dream, a vision of the night, when deep sleep falls upon men," and so on, "then He opens the ears of men." And this matter is visibly apparent, that according to what a person is, so his dreams prove true; and sometimes he sees visions of the upper world and speaks with the dead and recognizes them, and they reveal to him the matter of the Garden of Eden and Gehinnom, as several incidents have occurred in our time - and I have not come, in this composition, to elaborate on the telling of these incidents.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:57: And they say, of blessed memory (Berachot, chapter 2, page 14b), that one who goes seven days without a dream is called wicked; in these words: Rabbi Yona said in the name of Rabbi Zeira: whoever lodges [i.e., sleeps] seven days without a dream is called wicked, as it is said (Proverbs 19:23), "and satisfied [save'a], he shall lodge, not visited by evil" - do not read "save'a" [satisfied] but "sheva" [seven] - to this point. And Rashi, of blessed memory, explains that because he is wicked, they do not watch over him from Heaven to visit him with a dream. And it seems to me that because his soul does not ascend above, therefore it does not come to him - for he is likened to the spirit of an animal, which descends below to the earth.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:58: And so too, through dreams the decrees decreed in the upper world become known - and Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Zohar, Parashat Shemot, page 6b) that when there are righteous people in the generation, they inform the head of the generation of the decree, and if not, [they inform] people lacking understanding, or children; in these words: Rabbi Chiya said, thirty days before strength comes to the world, on earth, or before a breaking comes upon the people, on earth, that matter is proclaimed in the world; and sometimes that matter is handed over into the mouth of children, and sometimes to those people who have no understanding, and sometimes that matter is handed over into the mouths of birds, and they proclaim it in the world, and there is no one who pays heed to them. When the people are meritorious, that matter is handed over to those meritorious heads of the world, so that they may inform them and they may return to their Master; and when they are not meritorious, it is as I said - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:59: Further, among the things a person must discern with his intellect, the providence of the Holy One, blessed be He, over Israel, is when he discerns the matter of wisdom given by Him, blessed be He, to those fit for it - as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, say: one who sees the sages of Israel blesses, "blessed is He who has given a portion of His wisdom to those who fear Him." And we have already seen here in Safed, in the Upper Galilee, sages for whom it was fitting to recite this blessing. And we have also seen sages who were expert in the wisdom of physiognomy, to tell a person everything he did, whether good or evil - and these certainly merited this wondrous wisdom, close to the holy spirit, only from the side of their deeds and piety.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:60: Further, of this category of contemplation is the wisdom of Kabbalah, in the working of the holy Names, which perform several actions - the Name of 42 and the Name of 72 - and so Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains (Beha'alotcha 151a) concerning the Name of 72, in these words: and with this Name is the binding of the fathers - ways are found for judgment and mercy, for assistance, for kindness, for fear, for Torah, for life, for death, for good and for evil. Happy are the righteous who know the ways of the Torah and know how to walk in the Torah of the holy King - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:61: And although it is true that it is not fitting for every person to use the holy Names - for who is fit to use the king's scepter but one who is close to the king - nevertheless we certainly know, without doubt, that one who knows how to use them, and is fit for this, performs awesome deeds, as I have seen, and as I have heard from the mouth of one who performed with them. And the Name of 72 is that which emerges from the verses "vayisa, vayavo, vayet" (Exodus 14:19-21), and it is the Name through which the sea was split, and therefore it is mentioned here. And further, there is the Explicit Name, which is the Name mentioned concerning the celestial spheres and their rotation, and it performs even greater wonders.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:62: Further, concerning the matter of contemplation that arouses a person to know his Creator and perform His Torah and His commandments, is in discerning the matter of death - for death in man is not like the death of other living creatures. For in other living creatures, if they die a natural death, the matter is from the side of illness, like an animal with a fatal defect [treifah] that cannot live, or the depletion of strength from old age; but this is not the matter of death in man - especially since we find death among small children, and likewise among young men whose strength is complete and who are in their full vigor and might, who die a sudden death without any preceding cause of illness at all; and especially in the illness of plague, which is sent from Him, blessed be He, for our sins from time to time, in which young and old and women die without cause - and in this illness the understanding of doctors becomes confused, none of them knowing good from bad, for we find that a doctor will say, concerning this illness, that the patient is well, and not an hour or two hours will pass before he dies. And many plague victims see the Angel of Destruction - some see him with a sword, some with a bow and arrows, and the like - as we have seen here in Safed, in the Upper Galilee, several times; for at a time of plague, from the side of the great judgment, the agents of judgment take on physical form so that they can be seen.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:63: And it is fitting that you know that death, for Israel in particular, is a supernal kindness to them, for the repair of their soul - and therefore it is said of Him (Psalms 145:17), "and pious [chasid] in all His works," for His essential works are the souls, which are literally the work of His hands. This is: when the Holy One, blessed be He, sees that this body, built jointly by husband and wife, since there is flesh in them from the side of the husks, has no further use for the repair of the commandments, He nullifies its existence in order to benefit the repair of its portion, which is the soul - for if there were no repair, what benefit would it be to the Holy One, blessed be He, to kill it and nullify its existence from the world? And why did He create it in the first place, if afterward, after some years, He would kill it? Rather, certainly this is the secret of reincarnation (which our Rabbis, of blessed memory, taught us, and Pythagoras agreed with them, though many disagree with this view) - in this His thoughts run deep, for "He devises means, that His banished one not remain banished from him," and the Holy One, blessed be He, brings the soul into this world to see whether it will improve its deeds, and leaves it until it does what it was sent to repair; and if it did not repair, they cut it off, like a tree that produces no fruit.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:64: And concerning the repair of death for Israel, that it is good for them, the prophet says (Jeremiah 18:6), "behold, as the clay in the potter's hand, so are you in My hand, O house of Israel" - for the potter, when he sees that the vessel will not turn out properly, nullifies that clay's form from what it was and shapes it into another, more improved form; and so, in the secret of reincarnation, it is said (Job 14:20), "You change his countenance, and send him away" - for if his countenance was originally the face of a lion, he comes in the second incarnation with the face of an ox, and so on for the rest; and always the divine intent is to repair the souls in the manner suited to them. For if this were not the divine intent regarding death, for the repair of souls, it would be difficult [to explain]: is it fitting that a craftsman who makes a completed work, and after finishing making it, having labored over it, should think to nullify it? Would we not say that his teeth are blunted [i.e., he has lost his edge] and that he is not of sound mind - unless one says that his nullifying it in this form is in order to make it in another, more improved form? And so is the matter with this craftsmanship that the Holy One, blessed be He, repaired, as it is said (Deuteronomy 32:6), "He made you and established you" - made and built with His supernal wisdom, from the totality of all the worlds - for if there were no repair in the nullification of its existence from this world, He would not put it to death.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:65: And everything is conducted according to how those below conduct themselves: if those below prepare their deeds properly, the Shechinah, called "the wheel" [galgal], through whom souls are reincarnated, tips to the right side, and the world is repaired; and if not, Heaven forfend, it tips to the left side - as the Sava explains (Zohar, Parashat Mishpatim, page 95b), that the scale never rests, and souls ascend, enter, and return; and he says further on: and when the people of the world conduct themselves toward the good side, the scale stands and tips toward the good side, and when they conduct themselves toward the evil side, it tips toward that side; see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:66: And along these lines, Rashbi, peace be upon him, also explains (there, Parashat Vayera, page 109b), on the verse (Job 37:12), "and it is turned about by His guidance, that they may do whatever He commands them," and so on: our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said, Rabbi Elazar said, "and it is turned about by His counsels" - the Holy One, blessed be He, brings about circumstances and causes deeds to occur in the world, to be established; and afterward, when people think that those deeds will be established, the Holy One, blessed be He, reverses them from how they were originally. "By His guidance" [betachbulotav] - it is written "betachbulato" [singular] - like this craftsman who makes clay vessels: while that wheel is turning before him, he thinks to make [a vessel] in this manner, and makes it; he thinks to make it in another manner, and makes it - he turns this vessel into that vessel, because that wheel is turning before him. So the Holy One, blessed be He, reverses His deeds that He performs - "betachbulato," lacking a yud [in a defective spelling] - and what is this? This is the court below, which is the wheel turning before Him, and therefore He turns vessels from this vessel to another vessel - and all this according to the deeds of people. If people improve their deeds, that turning wheel turns them to the right, and then deeds are done in the world to benefit them properly, and the wheel always turns on that right side, and the world is reincarnated/rolled along by it. If people come to do evil, "betachbulato," which always turns and stands turning to the right - the Holy One, blessed be He, turns it to the left side, and reverses the circumstances and vessels that were originally to that left side, and then the wheel turns and deeds are done in the world to harm people, and the wheel turns to that side until people repent to improve their deeds, and the wheel stands [poised] according to people's deeds - and therefore "betachbulato," according to their deeds, and it does not stand still always - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:67: And through this discourse, the saying of our Rabbis, of blessed memory, may be understood (Kiddushin, chapter 8, page 40b): a person should always view himself as half meritorious and half guilty, and the world as half meritorious and half guilty - if he performs one commandment, happy is he, for he has tipped himself and the whole world to the side of merit, and so on - and the tipping depends on the aforementioned scale, and it depends on the deeds of those below, as explained.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:68: And therefore one who repents in repentance does kindness with his own soul, his body, with the whole world - whom he tips to the side of merit - and with the Holy One, blessed be He. With his soul - by removing it from the judgment of Gehinnom and the other reckonings and judgments explained in the rest of the Gate of Fear, and from the judgment of reincarnation, which is hard for the soul. And with his body - that it not be cut off in the prime of its days, and they demand of him, why did you not repair your deeds - for perhaps you would have had a son who would be a halachic authority in Israel, as explained in the Sefer HaBahir. And with the Holy One, blessed be He - that he does not burden the Holy One, blessed be He, to execute upon him the judgment of death and reincarnation - for the Holy One, blessed be He, has no desire in the death of the wicked, but rather that they turn from their evil ways, for the judgment of reincarnation is very hard for the soul, and the Holy One, blessed be He, is merciful, and His way is to do good with His creatures, especially with His holy souls, which are a portion of Him, blessed be He, and He does not wish to uproot the soul from the place from which it was hewn, its original quarry, where its life-source stands - and this is like one who uproots a tree from its original place of planting and from its roots, where it lived, and transplants it elsewhere. And for this reason the Holy One, blessed be He, is patient with the wicked, [hoping] perhaps they will repent, for the choice is in their hands; and when He sees that they have not repented, then He uproots them in order to transplant them elsewhere. And they elaborate on this exposition in the Tikkunim (page 102b); see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:69: And therefore, the discerning person must contemplate the matter of death, as they say (Ecclesiastes 7:4), "the heart of the wise is in the house of mourning," "and let the living take it to his heart" (ibid. 7:2) - for he was not sent into this world to eat and drink like an animal, in the manner of fools, whose heart is in the house of feasting - for concerning this, what benefit is there in his creation? Are there not many of this kind among the idol-worshipping nations, who eat and drink and do their work and die, and as they came, so they go, and are not punished, because they have no soul and were not commanded concerning the commandments - unless they act wickedly, for then it is said of them (I Samuel 25:29), "and the souls of your enemies, He will sling out as from the hollow of a sling."
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:70: And Rashbi, peace be upon him, explains in the Song of Songs [passage] (Zohar Chadash, Song of Songs 70d) that one of the things for which a person gives a reckoning at his departure is whether he investigated and knew why his soul came into the world and what it came to repair; in these words: the wisdom a person needs is: one, to know and contemplate the secrets of his Master; and [one], to know his own body, and to recognize who he is and how he was created, and from where he comes and to where he goes, and how the repair of his body is to be repaired, and how he is destined to enter into judgment before the King of all; and one, to know and contemplate the secrets of his soul - who is that soul within him, and from where it comes, and for what purpose it comes into this body, a putrid drop, here today and in the grave tomorrow - to the extent relevant here.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:71: Further, concerning the matter of the repair of death for man, that it is a repair of his soul, Rashbi, peace be upon him, elaborates (Zohar, Parashat Terumah, page 150a); he raises a difficulty there concerning what they say, of blessed memory, on the verse "and God saw everything that He had made, and behold, it was very [me'od] good" - that "tov" [good] is the angel of life, and "me'od" is the Angel of Death, who is even better, because he obeys the command of his Master - and he elaborates in resolving this matter, concerning the Garden of Eden and the matter of Adam before his sin. And the summary of his intent on this matter is that through the sin of Adam, man is clothed in the coarse, material body that prevents the soul from gazing upon the supernal spiritual realms; and through death, he strips off this garment and clothes himself in a spiritual garment made from the deeds of Torah and the commandments that he engaged in in this world, and through them he merits to gaze upon and delight in the light of the supernal life. And he says: and the Holy One, blessed be He, does good with His creatures, that a person is not stripped of these garments until other, more precious and better garments than these are prepared for him - except for those wicked of the world who did not return in complete repentance to their Master, for they come into the world naked and return there naked - to this point. It follows that death is a repair for the righteous man, for through it he merits to be clothed in that spiritual garment; and for the wicked man, that out of fear of death he will repent, as we explained above this.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:72: And of this category of contemplation is that he should discern what we find, that several righteous men were not subject to the worm - and besides those mentioned in the baraita (Bava Batra 17a), we find Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Shimon, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, say (Bava Metzia, chapter 7, page 83), and Rashbi, peace be upon him, as is proven in the Zohar (Parashat Bereshit, page 4a); and so too, in the time of the Amoraim, Achai bar Yoshiah, as our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Shabbat, chapter 23, page 152b).
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:73: And even in our own time, in the kingdom of Fez, an incident of this kind occurred, and this was the incident: a certain pious man died outside his own town, in a village a day or two's journey away, and was buried there. After several years, the sons of that pious man went to bring his bones to be buried with the members of his family, and they found that his flesh had not decomposed except for one leg alone. And his elder son was troubled over the matter, for what reason that leg had decomposed, and he was worried lest the worm still be active in it, and he fasted; and his father came to him in a dream and said to him: know that the worm was active only in that leg, because he kicked a Torah master with it, but the rest of his body, with which he did not sin, the worm was not active in it and never will be. So I heard from an elderly sage who heard these words from the mouth of the son of the aforementioned pious man - and the son is still alive.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:74: And when a person considers this matter, that for this generation it is a great thing, and without doubt everything depends only on deeds, as they say (Avot 1:17), "not study but practice is the essential thing" - for there are several men of Torah who have not merited this - and everything depends on the extent to which a person purifies his soul and his deeds, so his physical matter is refined accordingly and the worm has no power over it. And it is possible that for this reason the righteous, at their death, are called "living" - for they purified their soul from the filth of the serpent, which is jealousy, desire, and honor - and therefore the cursed serpent, from whose side comes the worm, had no power over them, and the power of Torah and commandments, called "life," cleaved to that flesh to such an extent that the worm had no power over them.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:75: And this is the divine intent concerning the matter of death - that the sin of Adam be repaired, and the matter return to how it was at the time of creation, when the sphere of his heel dimmed the sphere of the sun - as they explain in the Midrash (Vayikra Rabbah, Parashat Acharei Mot 20:2), in these words: Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Menasya: the heel of Adam, the first man, would dim the sphere of the sun - how much more so the countenance of his face! And do not be astonished - it is the way of the world that a person makes one bag for himself and one for his household - for which of them does he make the finer one? Not for his own [household], but for his own [personal use, i.e., prioritizing his own]. So Adam, the first man, was created for the service of the Holy One, blessed be He, and the sphere of the sun was for the service of creatures - to this point. And so it is explained in the Tikkunim (page 10b); see there.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:76: And they further explain (Zohar, Parashat Chayei Sarah, Midrash HaNe'elam, page 121b): come and see, Rabbi Yehuda said, the image of Adam, the first man, and his beauty, was like the radiance of the supernal firmament that is above the rest of the firmaments, and like that light which the Holy One, blessed be He, has stored away for the righteous for the World to Come - to this point.
Reshit Chokhmah, Gate of Love 6:77: And concerning the matter of the resurrection of the dead, this matter will be repaired, as explained there. And so our Rabbis, of blessed memory, explain (Yalkut, Parashat Devarim, section 801): the righteous are destined, in the future to come, to be compared to the sun and the moon, and so on. And so they say in the Zohar, Parashat Bereshit (page 4a), concerning Rashbi, when Rabbi Chiya saw him, and it says there: he saw that they were being restored and renewed in their splendor and light, greater than the light of the splendor of the sun - to this point.
